page: Amazon Web Services m6in.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The server configuration includes 256 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI, VAES, SHA-NI cryptography acceleration, and a 54 MB L3 cache. The instance features no local storage and contains zero GPUs, relying exclusively on network-attached storage options paired with a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data reflects strong upper-quartile execution in PassMark CPU score (57,720.48), PassMark extended instructions (53,530.20), cryptographic processing (56,471.11), and database operations (26,418.28). In application testing, the configuration demonstrated top-tier throughput in Clang software compilation (41,747.0), ray tracing (59,178.0), and static web serving (44.25 GB/sec). Standard compute benchmarks like stress-ng single-core (1,893.89) and multi-core (61,940.75), as well as Geekbench overall metrics, placed in the median tier. DDR4 memory bandwidth achieved 167.4 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 67.59 GB/sec on writes.

Because the server includes zero local ephemeral disks, storage throughput relies entirely on network protocols across the 100 Gbps interface. This design provides high throughput for data transfer between network volumes and processing threads without consuming physical drive slots. The balanced hardware ratio and high network speed fit transactional database servers, large CI/CD build environments, static web serving clusters, and distributed enterprise microservices requiring consistent non-burstable CPU capacity.

The instance incorporates a high baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, though it provides no bundled local storage and zero GPU accelerators.
